environment.description: Same Go 1.21 microservice deployed on ECS Fargate. Signing operations are performed exclusively through a Thales Luna Network HSM 7 (firmware 7.8.2) connected via PKCS#11 interface over a dedicated PrivateLink endpoint. The HSM partition is configured with partition policy flag 0 (no key export) and the crypto officer role requires M-of-N authentication (2-of-3 smartcard quorum) for any policy changes. The HSM audit log streams to a separate CloudWatch log group with resource policy preventing deletion. The container's seccomp profile (deployed via ECS task definition seccompProfile field referencing an S3-hosted profile) restricts syscalls to a baseline set: read, write, open, close, stat, fstat, mmap, mprotect, munmap, brk, rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocedure, ioctl, access, pipe, select, sched_yield, mremap, msync, clone, execve, exit, wait4, fcntl, flock, fsync, fdatasync, getdents, getcwd, chdir, rename, mkdir, link, unlink, readlink, chmod, getuid, getgid, geteuid, getegid, getppid, getpgrp, setsid, socket, connect, accept, sendto, recvfrom, bind, listen, getsockname, getpeername, epoll_create, epoll_ctl, epoll_wait, futex, clock_gettime, exit_group, openat, newfstatat, set_tid_address, set_robust_list, prlimit64, getrandom, close_range, rseq. Notably ABSENT from the seccomp allowlist: fork, vfork, clone3, ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, and all *at variants except openat/newfstatat. The template execution in Go's html/template package calls reflect internally but cannot spawn subprocesses or read arbitrary files because (1) the seccomp profile blocks fork/clone3 preventing os/exec, and (2) the container filesystem is read-only (readonlyRootFilesystem: true in task definition) with only /tmp mounted as a tmpfs with noexec,nosuid,size=64m. Additionally, Go's html/template auto-escapes all pipeline outputs through contextual escaping functions (unlike text/template), meaning injected template directives that reference struct fields are rendered as escaped HTML strings rather than executable code. The combination of html/template's contextual auto-escaping, the restricted seccomp profile, and read-only filesystem means that even if an attacker controls the template structure, they cannot: (a) inject raw HTML/JS due to contextual escaping, (b) call methods that spawn processes due to seccomp, (c) write persistent payloads due to read-only fs. The HSM ensures no key material is extractable regardless of application-level compromise.

config.hsm: Thales Luna Network HSM 7, firmware 7.8.2, PKCS#11 via PrivateLink
config.hsm_partition_policy: flag 0 (no export), 2-of-3 M-of-N quorum for policy changes
config.network: Private subnet, ALB with no WAF, PrivateLink to HSM
